crossrefs.text: Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice from the herd or flock in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.
Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.
On the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. He said:
So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
And Noah did all that the Lordhad commanded him.

Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year. Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household. If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly. Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
“Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.

you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’” Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
But Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the LORDʼs salvation, which He will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the peopleʼs representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
He must not go near any dead body; he must not defile himself, even for his father or mother.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse. So they brought him to Moses. (His motherʼs name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
It must be eaten inside one house. You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
Do not leave any of it until morning; before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.
But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”

For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.

If a foreigner resides with you and wants to celebrate the LORDʼs Passover, all the males in the household must be circumcised; then he may come near to celebrate it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.
The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”
And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.

And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night. Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.

And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them, so that it came between the camps of Egypt and Israel. The cloud was there in the darkness, but it lit up the night. So all night long neither camp went near the other.
At morning watch, however, the LORD looked down on the army of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw their camp into confusion.
